evidence.eventual_fix_title: Fix memory leak in BackgroundCommandSenderHostedService by using CommandContext.CancellationToken
evidence.eventual_fix_problem_statement:
Fix memory leak in BackgroundCommandSenderHostedService by using CommandContext.CancellationToken ## Issue Memory leak was occurring when dispatching high volumes of workflows (~200/second), resulting in accumulation of `CancellationTokenSource` objects that weren't being properly disposed. Memory profiling showed thousands of these objects remaining in memory even after workflow queues were empty. ![Memory leak showing CancellationTokenSource accumulation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22cae843-d3e1-4485-98f0-1f43f3444829) ![Memory leak paths to root](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbc72033-5040-44d0-9a50-1cad91601e9d) ## Root Cause In `BackgroundCommandSenderHostedService.ReadOutputAsync()`, the hosted service's `cancellationToken` was being passed to individual command executions instead of using each `CommandContext`'s own `CancellationToken`. This created unnecessary token relationships/registrations that weren't being properly cleaned up. ## Solution Changed the command execution to use the context-specific cancellation token: ```diff - await commandSender.SendAsync(commandContext.Command, CommandStrategy.Default, commandContext.Headers, cancellationToken); + await commandSender.SendAsync(commandContext.Command, CommandStrategy.Default, commandContext.Headers, commandContext.CancellationToken); ``` ## Result After applying the fix, memory usage is significantly reduced as shown in the user's testing: ![Fixed memory usage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6bfc8e8-b6f3-4849-867f-94e5791b922f) ## Why This Works - Each `CommandContext` is created with its own `CancellationToken` that is properly scoped to that specific command operation - Using the hosted service's `cancellationToken` created token linking that prevented proper cleanup - The fix ensures each command uses its intended cancellation token, eliminating the memory leak while maintaining proper cancellation semantics ## Testing - ✅ Code builds successfully with no new errors - ✅ Integration tests pass - ✅ Verified no functional regressions - ✅ Minimal, surgical change (single line modification) Fixes #6449. > [!WARNING] > >
